Q: JUnit Test cases failing after upgrading to Gradle 9, Springboot 4 and Java 25 A:

This is probably due to changes in the web dependency of Spring Boot 4. Use spring-boot-starter-webmvc instead of spring-boot-starter-web and spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test for MVC tests. Next, execute ./gradlew dependencyInsight --dependency spring-web --configuration testRuntimeClasspath to see why the dependency 'spring-web' is not included. Also make sure that your Spring Cloud '2025.1.2' BOM is compatible with your Spring Boot 4 version.

Q: Can C++ "happens-before" order contradict physical wall-clock execution time? A:

Yes, it can. The key distinction is that C++ happens-before is a logical ordering relation, not a statement about physical wall-clock timing. An operation can be ordered before another by the language memory model even when the actual execution or observation timing looks different due to compiler reordering, CPU out-of-order execution, caching, or synchronization. So “A happens-before B” should be read as a guarantee about permitted program behavior and visibility—not as “A physically occurred earlier on a clock.”

Q: What Language Would be the Best Option to Learn as Somebody Mainly Interested in IT A:

Without any further context I recommend racket. It comes with its own environment DrRacket. Be advised though that many programmers frown on Lisp.

If you are interested in creating websites the obvious choice is JavaScript. A popular editor is Visual Studio Code.

If you are interested in understanding how computers work I'd recommend C. It's fairly low level and requires you to manage memory manually.

If you are interested in learning a language popular with employers I suppose Java is a safe bet, possibly C# as well. Read some ads to get an idea.

Another popular choice for beginners is Python.

I recommend to pick one and stick with it for some time (at least a year). After getting your feet wet you will have a better understanding what the limitations of the language are and can use that to guide your decision for the next language to learn. It's common for programmers to know several programming languages.

Q: Visual Studio Debugging: freeze current thread by code A:

Yes. On Windows, you can programmatically freeze a thread using SuspendThread() with a handle to that thread. To continue it later, call ResumeThread(). However, if a thread suspends itself, it cannot resume itself because it stops executing immediately; another thread must call ResumeThread().
like
HANDLE h = /* thread handle */;

SuspendThread(h); // freeze

ResumeThread(h); // continue
